# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-27

**Your own long-form went up today, “Did Hindus Kings Loot Temples?”: fix “Hindus” to “Hindu” in the title now and judge it on 30 November. The Churchill Short has to be written today to be recorded tomorrow, and at its recent pace the Indonesia long-form is days from becoming the channel's fifth breakout.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish a Short for Churchill's birthday on 30 November: what his War Cabinet was told about the Bengal famine in 1943, and what it decided.** (short, due 2026-11-30, open since 2026-11-24)  
   Why: Due in three days and not written. A ruler convicted by his own papers is the channel's best shape for subscribers: “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History” brings 12.7 per 1,000 views, and its lesson is “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.” That the birthday lifts it is a guess.  
   First step: Write it today: one dated 1943 War Cabinet document in sentence one, and no INA context in the first 10 seconds (it sank your 2025 Churchill Short at 0:05). Record 28 November; publish the morning of 30 November.
2. **Script and publish a follow-up long-form for the Indonesia video's viewers: why Bali stayed Hindu when Java converted.** (long, due 2026-12-02, open since 2026-11-19)  
   Why: The Indonesia long-form is the nearest breakout: 439 net subscribers by 24 November against the line of 500, at 3.8 per 1,000 views, nearly twice the Asia one's 2. A follow-up reaches those viewers while they still come every day. Bali as the subject is a guess from the comments.  
   First step: The transcript is in: at 0:19 the script left its hook for facts viewers already knew, and they left with it. Today pick the culprit and the dated act for sentence one, and stay inside it. Keep “Indonesia” in the title.
3. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Three days late with nothing on disk; it lapses at tomorrow's refresh. Correction: yesterday's brief said it would lapse today, but a decision lapses only when it is more than three days past due. Late, it keeps only its search value (“guru tegh bahadur history”), worth less than today's hours on Churchill.  
   First step: Nothing to do unless you will publish it today. Either way the Sati Short, already written, takes this slot in tomorrow's brief.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
18,400 subscribers, up 500 in a week, against 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 20,996, which needs 87 net a day; the last 7 days ran at 90.7, above that pace, but the channel is 2,314 behind the ramp, so on the 7-day rate November ends near 18,672, 2,324 short. Furthest behind is breakouts: none this month against 2,032 subscribers planned from them, and breakouts carry 63.6% of lifetime subscribers. The nearest is the Indonesia long-form (second decision); Analytics stops at 2026-11-24, so whether it has crossed the line is not known yet. Last week both videos you shipped were your own picks: the long-form beat its usual, the Short did not. Today's long-form is your pick too, so the decisions below are the dated Short and the one follow-up.

What's working
- “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” is the best subscriber-earner of this month's uploads: 3.8 net per 1,000 views on 123,006 views, and it pushed long-form views up 102.4% week over week. Over 28 days long-form earns 87.0% of the net subscribers videos bring.
- The 90-day window's best converter is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, 12.7 net per 1,000 views: a named historian convicted by his own record. Today's long-form has the same shape, a named historian checked against the inscriptions.
- Searchable names keep earning: “Why Is Ram Setu Called ADAM'S Bridge?” has 12,765 views and still draws a few hundred a day three weeks on, largely from people searching “ram setu” and “adams bridge”. The Churchill Short needs his name first in the title for the same reason.

What's wrong
- Viewers leave the Indonesia long-form early: average view is 27.8%, and 16 points of the audience go at 0:19. The transcript is in now and shows why: at 0:19 the script leaves its hook, the Malay Ramayana in which Ravana gets his powers from Allah, for what Indians already forward about Indonesia (“In India we love to share that its currency once featured Ganesha”). The channel's own lesson from the India Ramayana video: “When the hook names a conflict, the next sentence must stay inside it.” Test: the Bali script stays inside its opening act for the first 30 seconds.
- Long-form views overstate real viewing: only 41.6% of November's long-form views were engaged views, and over the 365-day window long-form now brings 7.1 subscribers per 1,000 views, below its usual range. The Asia Ramayana video brings 2 per 1,000 and the India one 1.2. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing. Test: judge today's long-form on 30 November by engaged views and subscribers, not by views.
- Shorts views fell 83.6% week over week (20,652 against 126,126) as the film Shorts aged. The newest, “Why Portuguese Goa Taxed Every Hindu's SHIKHA”, has 1,572 views and no subscribers yet; it loses viewers at 0:05 and again at 0:09, where the blame moves from the Portuguese to Aurangzeb (“The Portuguese were inspired by Aurangzeb”). Probable cause: two culprits in the first 10 seconds. Test: the Churchill and Sati Shorts keep one culprit through the first 15 seconds.
- The three Halley Kalyan clips that went up in the same minute on 3 November have 24, 97 and 264 views. Probable cause: three clips from one conversation competing with each other, each opening on talk rather than on something that happened. Test: the next interview clip goes out alone, a day clear of any other Short, opening on a dated fact.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-24. Long-form is found on Home: 264,982 of its 296,267 views over 28 days came through Home and the subscriptions feed, against 7,635 from search, so a long-form's title and thumbnail have to win on Home. Outside YouTube, WhatsApp sends the most viewers: 13,053 views over the 365-day window, 28x what Instagram sends.
- Indonesians are correcting the Indonesia video in its own comments: “Rama were never worshiped in Classical Nusantara... esp. in the Majapahit era”. The Bali script has to say what Majapahit's courts worshipped before it says what Bali kept.
- The most-liked objection under the Asia video names the Cholas: “ever heard of Chola Empire?”, and another viewer asks about Rajendra Chola and Srivijaya. That is the idea below.
- The Ramayana videos reach viewers outside India: a Burmese Buddhist writes that he is “still big fan of Ramayana”, and another viewer says the Asia video forgot Bagan in Myanmar.

## How they are reacting
The Indonesia long-form still holds the week's comments: viewers from Indonesia and Malaysia correcting and adding, anger at Islam as a whole, and pride in how far the Ramayana travelled.
- **Southeast Asian viewers correcting and adding** (mixed): "Hi Indonesian here. its great video but few correction probably needed."
- **Anger turning on Islam as a whole** (negative): "Gaslighting since 1000 years ago... way to go islam."
- **The Ramayana as India's reach abroad** (positive): "It is our softpower"
- **Sai Pallavi's Ravana remark still argued over** (mixed): "The irony of playing Sita and defending Ravana in return"
- **Colonial Shorts read as being about today** (mixed): "Same with today's Bureaucracy too."

Requested topics
- Rajendra Chola's raid on Srivijaya
- Bagan and the Ramayana in Myanmar
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one
- Hindi versions of the long-forms

## Competitors
The watchlist's month is still the Ramayana film on channels far larger than Itiha. Two openings are worth taking for this week's scripts.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Diwali is South Asian... wait.. what?"
  Why it worked: 161,201 views at 30.8x its usual, the watchlist's biggest jump this month. Sentence one is the other side's claim, quoted flat; sentence two is one word: “Diwali is not a Hindu festival. It's a South Asian festival. What?”
  Steal: For Churchill: open on what his admirers say of him, then the 1943 document that answers it.
- **Project SHIVOHAM**: "She's NOT Subhadra? The Forgotten Ancient Goddess"
  Why it worked: 262,617 views at 7.2x its usual. It opens on a picture millions already hold and breaks it at once: “At Puri Jagannath, millions worship Jagannatha, Balarama, and the goddess between them. Who is she?”
  Steal: For Bali: the Bali temple every Indian has seen forwarded, then, in the next sentence, the dated act that explains why it is still Hindu.

Gaps
- Mohak Mangal's “Reality of Aurangzeb” has no long-form answer from the primary sources, on the watchlist or on Itiha, though the channel's two biggest Shorts ever are about Aurangzeb. Worth a long-form when the 26 December Anandpur date comes due.
- The Emissary's Short “How Did Indian War Elephants Actually Work?” ran far above that channel's usual; nothing on Itiha covers it. It has no culprit, so it is a gap, not a pick.

## Trending now, make this
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Sati ban, 4 December  
  Signal: Bentinck's regulation against sati in Bengal is seven days out, and your Short “The Year Britain Banned Sati, Englishmen Were Selling Their Wives” is written and sourced, not recorded. (Calendar, script on disk)  
  Make: It takes the Tegh Bahadur slot tomorrow. Record by 2 December and publish the morning of 4 December, with “Sati” in the title because that is what people search. First settle the line the script itself flags: “never wrote a law” needs checking, since courts acted on wife sales under other charges. The Ayodhya inscription Short, written on 1 November, follows on the morning of 6 December.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: 14 December 1971: the killing of Bengal's intellectuals  
  Signal: Seventeen days out, two days before Vijay Diwas. The research step falls on 30 November. (Calendar)  
  Make: From 30 November, find who drew up the list and who carried it out, with names and the date. Script a Short for the morning of 14 December with the culprit in sentence one, about two minutes long to bring subscribers, judged on day three.
- **watch, short, 3/5**: Timur's sack of Delhi, 17 December 1398  
  Signal: Twenty days out; the research step falls on 3 December. The same date marks the Saunders killing by Bhagat Singh and his comrades. (Calendar)  
  Make: From 3 December, check what Timur's own memoir says about the prisoners killed before the battle, and whether historians accept the memoir. If it holds, a Short for the morning of 17 December that opens on his own words. The channel's earlier Timur Short brought no subscribers, so this is a guess. Skip the Saunders date: freedom-fighter biographies are the channel's weakest Shorts.
- **watch, skip, 1/5**: Constitution Day  
  Signal: Constitution of India readership is 2.73x its usual in Hindi, and #ConstitutionDay led India's X trends. (Wikipedia, X)  
  Make: Skip. The day has passed, and the channel's Short on it, “Why Is Lord Rama in the Original Constitution of India?”, brought no subscribers (0 per 1,000).

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [2/5, short] **The Chola Navy That Sailed to Sumatra in 1025**  
  Empire mechanism: a naval raid on the kingdom that controlled the sea route to China; check the Tanjore inscription before scripting; Contested history: it answers the Asia video's own line that India never sent a soldier, which viewers are disputing in its comments  
  source: The most-liked objection under the channel's biggest long-form; set its Related video to “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?”. That it brings subscribers is a guess.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,547 followers, up only 6 in the last 7 days, 0.9 a day. November's feed posts cannot be judged yet, because their follows keep arriving for about three weeks. The latest reel, on British officers' pay, reached 1,124 with a skip rate of 59.4%, worse than the reel median of 54.0%. Carousels still do the growing: their median reach is 3.68x that of reels.

Do more
- Write carousels that correct the record  
  50 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 21 for the other lanes (41 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 11.0k, conversion 3.77 vs 1.97 per 1k. 492 followers a month at stake.
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 36 followers (91 posts); outside the band, 12 (16 posts). Pooled rate 2.89 vs 1.85 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 423 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  18 of 104 rated posts are shared above the median (24.7/1k) but convert below it (2.1/1k): median 9.8k reach for a median 9 followers. The 34 posts that do both average 278 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 944 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  88 single images all time: 86.0k reach between them and 122 followers, 1.4 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 159.6. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 93 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **now**: Fix the title of today's long-form: “Did Hindus Kings Loot Temples?” should read “Did Hindu Kings Loot Temples?”.  
  It has 20 views so far, so almost nobody has seen the misspelling yet, and “hindu kings” is what a searcher would type. Fix it before Home and search start testing it widely.
- **this_week**: Upload the Malay Ravana Short: title starting “Ravana”, Related video set to the Indonesia long-form, its link in the pinned comment, and the Malay “Hikayat Seri Rama” named on screen.  
  Written since 19 November to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form, which still brings subscribers every day but fewer than in its first week. Whether a Short sends viewers on is a guess.
- **this_week**: Answer the fact-check and the Indonesian viewer's correction under the Indonesia video with sources (/replies drafts them), and pin a correction if a point is wrong.  
  The Bali video goes to the same viewers; a fix made before it protects it.
- **later**: Set GA4_PROPERTY_ID in .env.  
  Without it the brief cannot read itiha.info; Search Console shows only searches for the name “itiha”.
